ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is the input terminal Ui, with the upper end marked “+” and the lower end marked “-”; the upper-left node is connected to the upper-right node through a diode. The vertical-line end of the diode (bar, cathode mark) is on the side of the left input terminal. The upper-right node is connected downward to a 3 kΩ resistor, then connected to a power-supply branch marked 5 V and returned to the bottom common terminal; the output voltage indicated by the vertical arrow on the right is U0, and what is measured is the voltage of the upper-right node relative to the bottom node. Reasoning: The problem statement gives Ui = 3 V, and the ideal diode forward voltage drop is 0 V. If the diode does not conduct, the 5 V power supply on the right side will pull the output node through the resistor to a potential higher than 3 V, therefore the potential of the diode anode on the right side is higher than the potential of the cathode on the left side, and the diode conducts forward. When the ideal diode conducts, the voltage drop is 0 V, so the output node is clamped to the input-node potential, U0 = Ui = 3 V.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, assuming the diode is ideal with a forward voltage drop of 0 V, what is the value of \(U_0\) when \(U_i = 3\text{ V}\)?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: identify the right-hand node above the resistor as U0, the left-hand top node as Ui, and note the diode orientation with the bar on the input side. From the text take Ui = 3 V and ideal diode forward drop = 0 V. Since the resistor/5 V branch tends to pull the output node up above 3 V, the diode conducts. With zero diode drop, the output node is clamped to the input node, so U0 = Ui = 3 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram and label the output node on the right of the diode, above the 3 kΩ resistor. From the text set Ui = 3 V and use an ideal diode. Test the OFF state: with the diode open, no current flows in the 3 kΩ branch, so the output node would sit at the 5 V source level. That would put the diode’s right/anode side at 5 V and left/cathode side at 3 V, forward-biasing it, so OFF is impossible. Therefore the diode is ON; with 0 V drop the output node equals the input node, giving U0 = 3 V.
